liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (3 reviews): Scarlet slows to a crawling groove before breaking into Fire and building back up, with the crowd roaring; Garcia's solos in Scarlet climb higher and higher as the crowd goes wild [19][28][30]
- **Fire on the Mountain** (1 review, 1 other source): In the transition to Fire the band nearly stops while Bill and Mickey play with the timing; A short two-minute jam occurs between Fire on the Mountain and Playin' in the Band [15][30]
- **Morning Dew** (2 reviews): The Wheel into Playin' reprise into Morning Dew is the reviewer's highlight of the show; Reviewer finds the Dew mind-blowing and one of their all-time favorites [25][30]
- **Bertha** (1 review): Reviewer finds the first two songs of the first set transporting [24]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Early in Jack Straw the vocals are partly drowned out by the audience; reviewer has heard better versions [20]
- **Althea** (1 review): Reviewer calls this the best Althea they have heard [20]

## Setlist highlights

- **intro jam**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [31]

## The recordings

- **gd1983-06-18.beyer-m88.morrone.119437.flac2448** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 177 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [1]. Said about its sound: The PA mix gets better after the first two songs [1]
- **gd83-06-18.aud.gardner.4605.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 171 min; rated 3.93/5 by 14 [4]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds this audience recording poor and thinks it sounds the same as the other copy from the same taper; Reviewer admits the audience tape quality is mediocre, but the show's energy still comes through; Recording quality is mediocre, but the crowd noise suits the high-energy show [22][24][28]
- **gd1983-06-18.148044.akg.d330bt.senn421.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 168 min; rated 3.67/5 by 3 [9]
- **gd1983-06-18.142271.beyer201.executive-crew.holbrook.flac2448**: audience recording; 20 songs; 158 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [11]
- **gd1983-06-18.154660.S2.Senn441-FRB-PCM-DAT.Silberman-Ammons-Noel.t-flac16**: source not stated; 11 songs; 106 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [15]

## Around the show

- Garcia played with notable energy that night, and the audience was fired up throughout [19]
- Reviewer's first concert; they later saw the band over thirty times and still rank this the best [24]
- Reviewer hitched from Boston; the parking lot filled up Saturday, with people inhaling whippets and the town overwhelmed by the crowd [26]
- Hells Angels rode their motorcycles around the crowds, and the reviewer nearly got caught by a state trooper [26]
- Reviewer hitched from Boston; the parking lot filled up Saturday, with people inhaling whippets and the town overwhelmed by the crowd [27]
- Hells Angels rode their motorcycles around the crowds, and the reviewer nearly got caught by a state trooper [27]
- Uploader notes a very unusual segue between Morning Dew and Throwing Stones [11]
- Scarlet > Fire and Playin' are good but cannot match the 10/6/84 versions, according to the reviewer [25]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1983-06-18.beyer-m88.morrone.119437.flac2448**: taped by Joe Morrone; transferred by Andrew F.; source: AUD: 2x Beyer M-88's > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX-90s, recorded from inside the pavilion, directly behind the soundboard area, taped by Joe Morrone. [1]. Also: Beyer M88 recording by Morrone, with patches from another source (ID-103293) in Playin', the Space segment and Touch [1]
- **gd83-06-18.aud.gardner.4605.sbeok.shnf**: source: Sennheiser 421's> Sony D-5 taped by Jim Wise [4]
- **gd1983-06-18.148044.akg.d330bt.senn421.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Chris Hecht; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Chris Hecht's Master Audience Cassettes; (2) AKG D330BT mics + (1) Sennheiser 421 > Fostex Mixer > Sony D5M [9]. Also: Jim Wise and Charlie Miller's Sennheiser 421 source supplies crowd, Bertha and Scarlet openings, Deal ending, and patches in Drums/Space and NFA transition [9]
- **gd1983-06-18.142271.beyer201.executive-crew.holbrook.flac2448**: taped by Executive Crew Fran Walsh Kyle Holbrook Mike Yacavone Olvy Johnson Rick Cantor; transferred by Kyle Holbrook; source: flac24/48 Master: AUD MC Beyer M201's X-Y 8'up > Sony TCD5M no dolby Maxell MX90 x 2.First Gen patch: [Same mics]Sony TCD5M no dolby Maxell UDXLII 90Cassette… [11]. Also: Master tape was accidentally overtaped from partway through Big River to the end of Althea, from a wrong tape side at a swap [11]
- **gd1983-06-18.154660.S2.Senn441-FRB-PCM-DAT.Silberman-Ammons-Noel.t-flac16**: taped by Recorded by Jeff Silberman PCM to DAT Transfer by Jeff Silberman; transferred by DAT Transfer by John Ammons Edited & Mastered (Adobe Audition) by Joe Noel November 05, 2021; source: Source: Sennheiser 441 > Technics 14 bit PCM > DAT Location: Front Row Balcony [15]. Also: Second-set-only Sennheiser 441 digital recording; Jeff skipped set one because rain threatened his new gear [15]

claims.text: Scarlet slows to a crawling groove before breaking into Fire and building back up, with the crowd roaring
Garcia played with notable energy that night, and the audience was fired up throughout
Reviewer calls this the best Althea they have heard
Early in Jack Straw the vocals are partly drowned out by the audience; reviewer has heard better versions
Reviewer finds this audience recording poor and thinks it sounds the same as the other copy from the same taper
Reviewer's first concert; they later saw the band over thirty times and still rank this the best
Reviewer admits the audience tape quality is mediocre, but the show's energy still comes through
Reviewer finds the first two songs of the first set transporting
The Wheel into Playin' reprise into Morning Dew is the reviewer's highlight of the show
Scarlet > Fire and Playin' are good but cannot match the 10/6/84 versions, according to the reviewer
Reviewer hitched from Boston; the parking lot filled up Saturday, with people inhaling whippets and the town overwhelmed by the crowd
Hells Angels rode their motorcycles around the crowds, and the reviewer nearly got caught by a state trooper
Reviewer hitched from Boston; the parking lot filled up Saturday, with people inhaling whippets and the town overwhelmed by the crowd
Hells Angels rode their motorcycles around the crowds, and the reviewer nearly got caught by a state trooper
Garcia's solos in Scarlet climb higher and higher as the crowd goes wild
Recording quality is mediocre, but the crowd noise suits the high-energy show
Reviewer calls this the benchmark Scarlet > Fire, with an especially rowdy, powerful jam in Scarlet
In the transition to Fire the band nearly stops while Bill and Mickey play with the timing
Reviewer finds the Dew mind-blowing and one of their all-time favorites
The PA mix gets better after the first two songs
Beyer M88 recording by Morrone, with patches from another source (ID-103293) in Playin', the Space segment and Touch
Master recording from Chris Hecht, transferred by Charlie Miller; AKG D330BT and Sennheiser 421 gear listed
Jim Wise and Charlie Miller's Sennheiser 421 source supplies crowd, Bertha and Scarlet openings, Deal ending, and patches in Drums/Space and NFA transition
Uploader notes a very unusual segue between Morning Dew and Throwing Stones
Master tape was accidentally overtaped from partway through Big River to the end of Althea, from a wrong tape side at a swap
Beyer 201 microphones used; recording credited to Executive Crew and Holbrook
Second-set-only Sennheiser 441 digital recording; Jeff skipped set one because rain threatened his new gear
A short two-minute jam occurs between Fire on the Mountain and Playin' in the Band
